Name: AI Weather - All Sky Camera Monitor
Author: Michele Bergo

short.EN: AI-powered all-sky camera weather monitoring with automatic safety protection for unattended imaging sessions

long.EN:
Protect your equipment and imaging sessions with intelligent, real-time weather monitoring powered by AI vision models. AI Weather watches the sky so you don't have to.

🌩️ REAL-TIME WEATHER MONITORING:
• Automatic Sky Analysis: AI vision models analyze your all-sky camera images to determine cloud coverage, detect rain and fog
• Continuous Protection: Periodic image capture and analysis runs in the background during your entire imaging session
• Instant Alerts: Weather status updates in real-time with detailed condition reports and cloud coverage percentages
• Live Preview: See exactly what the AI sees with the built-in camera preview panel

📷 3 FLEXIBLE CAPTURE MODES:
• RTSP Stream: Live video from network IP cameras (Dahua, Hikvision, etc.) with real-time preview and snapshot extraction
• HTTP Image Download: Periodic image download from any URL — works with indi-allsky, AllSky, web cameras, and any HTTP-accessible image
• Folder Watch: Monitors a local directory for the latest image saved by any camera software — perfect for USB cameras or custom setups

🤖 5 AI PROVIDERS (Free to Advanced):
• Local (FREE, Offline): Built-in heuristic analysis using brightness, color distribution, and edge detection — no internet needed, no API costs
• Google Gemini (free API tier): fast and capable Flash/Pro vision models
• Ollama / Custom (FREE, Local): Any vision model on a local OpenAI-compatible server (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, LocalAI) — no API key, full privacy
• OpenAI: GPT-4o and GPT-4o Mini for high-accuracy cloud and weather analysis
• Anthropic Claude: excellent at detailed image understanding
(GitHub Models was retired by GitHub on July 30, 2026 and no longer works.)

🛡️ SAFETY FEATURES:
• Two Cloud Thresholds: a high one that turns the state Unsafe and a low one that lets it return to Safe, so a sky hovering around a single number does not flip the sequence back and forth
• Rain Detection: Rain (including lens droplets) immediately triggers Unsafe — regardless of cloud threshold
• Fog Detection: Fog conditions immediately trigger Unsafe — protects optics and prevents wasted exposures
• Automatic Fallback: If the cloud AI provider fails, times out, or loses connectivity, the plugin falls back to local offline analysis
• 60-Second Timeout: All AI providers have a 60-second timeout to prevent indefinite hangs during analysis
• ASCOM SafetyMonitor Integration: Outputs a status file compatible with the ASCOM Generic File SafetyMonitor for third-party software integration
• Fail-Safe Data Expiry: the verdict expires. If no analysis succeeds within the Maximum data age (configurable; automatic means three check intervals and never below 10 minutes), the monitor reports Unsafe instead of holding the last known state - a camera that dies while the sky is clear no longer reports Safe indefinitely. Disconnecting clears the verdict too, so a reconnect starts Unsafe until the first successful analysis
• External ASCOM Safety Monitor: pick a second safety device with the ASCOM chooser and its verdict is combined with AND - imaging is Safe only when both the sky analysis and that device say so. Pair all-sky cloud, rain and fog detection with a rain sensor or a humidity and dew-point monitor. Any failure to reach it reports Unsafe
• It says WHY: the panel names the reason for the current state - a cloudy sky, data too old with the age and the limit, or an unreachable external device - instead of leaving it in the log

🧠 IT LEARNS YOUR SITE:
• Site notes: a free-text field for what the AI cannot guess about your location, in your own words - "clouds to the south are lit orange by the city and can look like overcast", "in daylight the sun reflects off the dome and creates a hazy halo". Sent with every analysis, for every provider. It steers interpretation only: the thresholds, the safety rules and the response format stay with the built-in prompt
• Daily sky digest into the shared knowledge wiki: what the sky did is filed into the same local markdown wiki the AI Assistant plugin reads, so a question about last night can be answered from what was actually observed
• Disable model thinking (Ollama, on by default): newer local models reason at length before answering, which took analyses from 14 to 78 seconds on the same image and past the timeout. Requests ask them not to

⚙️ EASY SETUP:
1. Configure your all-sky camera source (RTSP URL, HTTP URL, or watched folder path)
2. Choose an AI provider and enter your API key (or use Local for zero-config offline analysis)
3. Set your cloud coverage safety threshold
4. Connect the safety monitor under Equipment → Safety Monitor → All Sky Camera Safety Monitor
5. Start monitoring — the plugin automatically protects your sequences

💡 BEGINNER-FRIENDLY:
• Start with Local (offline) mode — no API keys needed, works out of the box
• Upgrade to Google Gemini (free API tier) or a local Ollama vision model for AI-powered analysis
• Detailed activity log shows every analysis result for easy troubleshooting
• Works with any all-sky camera that provides RTSP, HTTP, or file-based output

⚡ PRO FEATURES:
• Custom Analysis Intervals: Configure how often the sky is analyzed (seconds between captures)
• Multiple Camera Support: Point to different camera sources as needed
• Robust Error Handling: Automatic recovery from network failures, API errors, and camera disconnects
• Detailed Logging: Every analysis result is logged with timestamp, provider, cloud percentage, and safety status
• Seamless NINA Integration: Works directly with NINA's safety monitor system to pause or abort sequences when conditions deteriorate

Transform your all-sky camera into an intelligent weather guardian. Focus on imaging while AI Weather keeps watch over your equipment and data.

Changes: The two cloud coverage thresholds now explain themselves in the options panel. The High one turns the status Unsafe, the Low one is what lets it come back to Safe, and between the two the status does not change - which is the whole point of having two, so a sky sitting right at the limit cannot flip the sequence back and forth

The Low threshold had never been documented anywhere. A user spent a session stuck on Unsafe with a clear sky in the log because his was set far below what his sky normally reads; the README now also says how wide the band should be (5 to 15 points) and what happens at either extreme

New icon: the same monochrome cloud-and-star mark the plugin already used in N.I.N.A.'s imaging tab strip. The old one was white on a transparent background, which left it invisible against a light theme

The plugin description now describes the plugin. The two safety features added in 1.15.0.0 - the verdict that expires when no analysis succeeds, and the external ASCOM safety monitor combined with AND - were missing from it, as were the site notes, the daily digest into the shared knowledge wiki, the option to stop local models reasoning at length, and the fact that there are two cloud thresholds rather than one

Removed AIWeatherOptionsView.xaml, a second options page that nothing referenced and N.I.N.A. never displayed. It still offered Gemini 1.5 and Claude 3.5 and a GitHub token, and it had already cost one feature: the external ASCOM safety monitor was built there, on a page nobody could reach, and had to be built again on the page that is actually shown

FAIL-SAFE: the safety state now expires. A failed capture used to leave the previous verdict standing, so a camera that died while the state was Safe kept reporting Safe indefinitely. If no analysis succeeds within the new Maximum data age (configurable; 0 = automatic, three check intervals and never below 10 minutes), the monitor reports Unsafe. Disconnecting also clears the verdict, so a reconnect starts Unsafe until the first successful analysis

External ASCOM Safety Monitor is now actually wired in: enable it and pick a device with the ASCOM chooser, and its verdict is combined with AND — imaging is Safe only when both the sky analysis and the external device say so. Any failure (not configured, driver missing, connection lost, read error) reports Unsafe. Previously the client class existed but was never instantiated, its settings were never read, and its UI was on a page the plugin does not show
The panel now says WHY the state is what it is: a cloudy sky, stale data with the age and limit, or an unreachable external device. That reason previously existed only in the log

RTSP: the username typed in the panel was never saved to the settings (only the password was), so the safety monitor connected with no credentials and the stream failed to open; the field was also blanked by the next settings sync. It is now persisted the moment it is entered

RTSP: credentials are percent-encoded before being placed in the URL. A password containing @, : or / — common in camera accounts — produced a malformed URL and a stream that would not open, with nothing in the log pointing at the password
The exported Safe/Unsafe status file and the Safe sequencer symbol now carry the same combined state NINA acts on; the file used to recompute its own verdict and could disagree
README rewritten around what actually ships, including a table of exactly what makes the state unsafe

New optional 'Site notes' field in the options: free text about your site or camera that is appended to the analysis prompt of every provider. Every location has visual quirks a general prompt cannot anticipate — clouds lit orange by a nearby city that read as overcast, a daylight sun reflection off the dome that reads as haze — and this is where that local knowledge enters the analysis

The notes steer interpretation only: the classification thresholds, the safety rules and the response format stay with the built-in prompt. Empty by default, so the prompt is unchanged for anyone who does not use the field

Shared knowledge wiki: the plugin now appends a compact daily sky digest (condition and safety CHANGES only, not one line per polling cycle) to %LOCALAPPDATA%\NINA\llmwiki\raw\ — the same local second brain the AI Assistant plugin consults and the nina.autopilot ingest agent consolidates into observing-site pages. Append-only and fully local
Options panel: button rows are now consistently left-aligned; the Folder Path browse row matches the other rows

Ollama: new 'Disable model thinking' option (on by default). Newer models (Gemma 4, Qwen 3.x, DeepSeek) reason at length before answering by default — analyses took 5x longer (77.6s vs 14.2s measured on the same image) and blew past the timeout. Requests now send reasoning_effort 'none'
Ollama: the response parser now recovers answers that land in a reasoning field instead of content (the 'no JSON tokens' error), strips inline think blocks, and accepts prose around the JSON

The AIWeather category now appears in the sequencer Symbols sidebar right at N.I.N.A. startup (3.3+), with blank values until the first analysis fills them - previously it only appeared after the first completed analysis, which read as 'nothing there' before connecting the safety monitor
The 'symbol broker not present' notice on N.I.N.A. versions before 3.3 is now logged once instead of on every monitoring cycle

GitHub Models provider marked as retired: GitHub shut the service down for everyone on July 30, 2026. No more failed network calls - analyses fall back to the Local heuristic with a clear explanation, and the options panel says why and where to go (Ollama/Custom local, Google Gemini free tier, OpenAI)

Gemini defaults refreshed: fallback model is now the gemini-flash-latest alias (always points to Google's latest stable Flash, cannot expire); static list updated to the current generation - Gemini 1.x/2.0 were shut down by Google
Google Gemini is now the recommended getting-started provider in the docs

Advanced Sequencer symbols (N.I.N.A. 3.3+): every analysis publishes Cloud, Confidence, Condition, Rain, Fog and Safe under an 'AIWeather' category in the sequencer's Symbols sidebar, usable in expressions and message templates
Symbol values refresh on every monitoring cycle and are blanked when the safety monitor disconnects, so expressions never act on a stale reading
On N.I.N.A. versions before 3.3 the plugin behaves exactly as before (integration is detected at runtime; minimum version stays 3.0)
